blogs.title: The Silent Hypoxia: When 'Ondine's Curse' Hides in the Posterior Fossa
blogs.description: Explore the terrifying pathophysiology of acquired central hypoventilation in Chiari Malformation Type I (CMI). This post analyzes why patients can experience severe oxygen desaturation (down to 70%) without the subjective sensation of dyspnea ('air hunger'). We discuss the dissociation between voluntary and automatic respiratory drives, the interruption of afferent brainstem pathways preventing cortical awareness of hypoxia, and why this presentation mimics congenital central hypoventilation syndrome despite a structural etiology.

blogs.title: Beyond GERD: Why Unexplained Dysphagia Demands a Brain Scan
blogs.description: Challenge the reflexive workup for choking episodes. This post examines the high yield of neurological etiologies—specifically CMI—in patients presenting with neurogenic dysphagia affecting solids and liquids equally, despite normal upper endoscopies and laryngoscopies. We review the statistics linking persistent dysphagia to CMI and provide a framework for when to pivot from GI/Otolaryngology referrals to neuroimaging in patients with 'negative' swallow studies.

blogs.title: The Crowded Foramen Magnum: Re-Reading Old Scans Can Save Lives
blogs.description: A deep dive into diagnostic error reduction through image stewardship. Using this 14-year case trajectory, we illustrate how reviewing historical CT scans (even those originally read as 'normal') can uncover critical findings like a crowded foramen magnum or subtle tonsillar descent. The post discusses the evolution of radiological criteria for CMI, the spectrum from incidental variant to pathological syndrome, and strategies for integrating historical imaging reviews into modern diagnostic algorithms.

blogs.title: The Vertex Allodynia Clue: Decoding Scalp Pain in Chiari Syndrome
blogs.description: Move beyond classic Valsalva-induced occipital headaches. This post investigates the unique presentation of vertex pain, cutaneous allodynia (pain from hair touching), and 'burning vertex syndrome' as potential red flags for brainstem compression. We differentiate these symptoms from primary headache disorders like nummular headache or occipital neuralgia alone, discussing how sensory processing deficits at the cervicomedullary junction might manifest as bizarre scalp sensitivities.

blogs.title: Sleep Study Pitfalls: Why Your AHI Might Be Underestimating Central Apnea in Chiari
blogs.description: Critique the limitations of standard sleep diagnostics in structural brainstem disease. We analyze how Type III sleep studies (lacking EEG) can significantly underestimate the severity of central sleep apnea by calculating indices based on total recording time rather than true sleep time. The post argues for advanced polysomnography with end-tidal capnography in suspected CMI cases to accurately capture central events that might otherwise be dismissed as 'mild' or 'benign.'
